actor_outcome: Admin's first real invoice posts to the books without being rejected
problem: Admins see their first real invoice rejected at posting: 125 of 321 first attempts (about 30 per 100 new accounts), Jan-May 2026
root_cause: Automation: the auto-matcher assigns unmatched tax rates to the ledger's default code without flagging them (mechanism trace: 22 of 30 rejected postings)
expected_value: Range 1 to 8 points on MET-0001 (reach x consequence, stats.md); the upper end assumes the correlational gap is causal
dependencies: INI-0004 (MET-0016 baseline, due 2026-12-07); rollout limited to the two ledgers with a change feed
risk: Admins see more unmatched items at connection; more work up front

actor_outcome: Admin gets an answer on mapping from the person who has the knowledge, without set-up stopping
problem: Admins see their first real invoice rejected at posting after entering a mapping they could not confirm (8 of 30 traced rejections carried an admin-edited pair)
root_cause: Policy: an adviser login costs a paid seat, so the accountant answers without access to the product or context
expected_value: 0 to about 4 points on MET-0001; lower bound 0 because the external-accountant segment is unsized (EVD-2026-0018)
feasibility: Medium: needs a scoped no-seat access path
dependencies: Segment size from INI-0004; prototype test with 8 accountants; Pricing and Packaging decision on adviser access
risk: Wider access to customers' books; accountants may still not engage

actor_outcome: Admin can see who holds an open mapping question and since when
problem: Admins wait on mapping answers with no date and enter a guess that is later rejected at posting
root_cause: Ownership and data: no record of an open mapping question and no role accountable for it (RACI check pending)
expected_value: Medium: makes the pause visible and measurable (MET-0015)
feasibility: High once an owner is named

actor_outcome: Admin can confirm that Ledgerly figures match the books before committing the team
problem: Admins do not bring their team in: 42 per 100 new accounts send no invite within 30 days; admins describe holding the team until one invoice is proven by hand
root_cause: Data without its consumer: the connector holds the posting result, but nothing shows the admin the ledger entry next to the invoice
expected_value: 0 to about 8 points on MET-0001, overlapping OPP-0001; reach is the 78% of accounts that attempt a sync, of whom 61% succeed at the first attempt; consequence unmeasured, so the lower bound is 0 (stats.md)
feasibility: High: data already returned by the connector
dependencies: INI-0004 (MET-0012 baseline, due 2026-12-07); MET-0005 baseline cut
risk: Surfaces old mismatches; short-term ticket rise

actor_outcome: Team can start invoicing while accounting set-up is still being confirmed
problem: Admins do not bring their team in (42 per 100 new accounts send no invite within 30 days) while accounting set-up is unconfirmed
root_cause: System coupling: every sent invoice posts to the ledger immediately, so an unconfirmed mapping makes each teammate's invoice a possible mis-post
expected_value: Potentially high; unmeasurable at small effect sizes (stats.md)

actor_outcome: Teammates start their first week with permissions that do not change under them
problem: Teammates hit unexplained blocks after admins apply approval rules late
root_cause: Leading candidate: the rules screen is only reached after invites are sent; alternatives are default permissions or admins not knowing rules exist
risk: Stricter defaults could slow teams that do not need approvals

actor_outcome: Admins blocked by mapping get expert help regardless of account size
problem: Admins of accounts under 10 seats who ask for live help are declined (58 of 187 requests); accepted requests wait a median 6 business days
root_cause: Policy: live help is allocated by seat count (10+) rather than by blocking risk
expected_value: Medium; overlaps OPP-0008 and depends on how many sessions INI-0001 removes
feasibility: Low this quarter: specialist capacity fixed at 6

problem: Stakeholder belief that invitations are caught by spam filters
root_cause: Email deliverability (stakeholder candidate; contradicted by 84% acceptance)
expected_value: Low: the gap is invites not sent
risk: Diverts effort from the real constraint

actor_outcome: Admins who have not started within the first week get going
problem: 11% of admins have no login within 7 days of signature
expected_value: Unknown: 45 of 412 accounts; their outcome not yet cut
feasibility: Research feasible: signature-date analysis and phone recruitment
risk: Acting without a cause risks repeating the 2025 checklist result
